court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: 2nd Joint Civil Judge Senior Division, Amravati in H.M.P. No.28 of 2014
case_name: Vinod @ Vinayak Bapurao Wankhade vs Sau. Sonali Vinayak Wankhade And 2

parties.respondent_defendant: Sau.Sonali Vinayak Wankhade, Nil; Ome Vinayak Wankhade, Nil; Harsh Vinayak Wankhade, Nil (through natural guardian mother)

facts_of_case: Petitioner challenged an order granting interim maintenance to respondents under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the petitioner to show that he has neglected to maintain his wife and children.
legal_principles.held: At this stage, what is necessary to be looked into is as to whether or not the petitioner though possessed of sufficient means to maintain his wife and children has neglected to so.

legal_principles.principle: A person's ability to earn income every day can be considered as sufficient means for maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The petitioner himself has produced on record a certificate from his employer, Kamal Electronics, Amravati. The certificate shows that the petitioner is working in the said shop on temporary basis and earning such sums as Rs. 150/- to Rs. 200/- per day subject to availability of work.

outcome.final_order: The impugned order was set aside and the matter was remanded back to the trial court for fresh consideration.

use_for_drafting: drafting a writ petition for interim maintenance
seeking consent for hearing in a family court
obtaining an oral judgment in a high court
